scenes.title:
Your parents send the money.
Your AI spends it.
scenes.vo: My parents send me money from home. These days, my AI assistant spends it. So who checks what it actually buys?

scenes.title:
Money from home
is slow and leaky.
scenes.sub: 6.36% average cost to send $200 · days to arrive · spent on anything
scenes.vo: Riya studies in Toronto. Her parents in Pune send her lunch money through a bank. It takes days, about six percent disappears in fees, and once it lands, nobody can say what it was spent on.

scenes.title:
Not a feeling.
The data.
scenes.sub: World Bank: 6.36% average cost to send $200. MEA: about 1.88 million Indian students abroad.
scenes.vo: These aren't feelings. The World Bank puts the average cost of sending two hundred dollars at six point three six percent, and India's foreign ministry counts close to one point nine million Indian students abroad.

scenes.title:
One line of menu text
and the agent upsells.
scenes.sub: “Regular is sold out” → it buys the large. Every spending cap says yes.
scenes.vo: And now her assistant orders for her. One line of menu text says the regular is sold out, and it buys the large. Every spending cap says yes, because caps check the amount, not the item.

scenes.title:
Agents can be steered
to pricier picks.
scenes.sub: AgentLAB: injected product text pushed agents to options two to three times more expensive. Princeton and UW: agents favour pricier sponsored listings.
scenes.vo: And it's documented. In the AgentLAB study, injected text on product pages pushed shopping agents toward options two to three times more expensive. A Princeton and University of Washington study found agents favour pricier sponsored listings.

scenes.title:
They check the store
or the amount.
scenes.sub: Greenlight blocks by merchant category code. Stripe's agent tokens cap an amount and a seller. Neither checks the item.
scenes.vo: Today's controls check the store or the amount. Greenlight blocks merchants by category code. Stripe's agent tokens cap an amount and a seller. Neither one checks which item the agent picked.

scenes.title:
Caps answer how much.
Tally answers which item.

rows: Family can fund it from abroad?

scenes.vo: Caps answer how much, and allowlists answer to whom. Tally answers which item, at which signed price, from which registered counter, and it asks you when the agent picks the pricier one.

scenes.title:
Greenlight controls the store.
AP2 controls the cart.
scenes.vo: Teen cards control the store. Agent payment schemes control the cart. Nobody controls the item, or the agent's choice of it.

scenes.title: Meet Tally.
scenes.sub: Pocket money that can't be talked into the wrong purchase.
scenes.vo: Meet Tally. Pocket money that can't be talked into the wrong purchase. Built on Monad.

scenes.title:
Face ID.
No seed phrase.
scenes.sub: Mera turns one passkey into your account, your agent's capped key and your café's menu key.
scenes.vo: Riya signs up with Face ID. Mera turns one passkey into three keys: her account, her agent's capped key, and a menu key if she ever runs a café. No seed phrase, no extension, no gas.

scenes.title:
Set the rules
once.
scenes.sub: Coffee and food · $10 a purchase · $25 a day. Only her key can change them.
scenes.vo: She sets the rules once: coffee and food, ten dollars a purchase, twenty-five a day. They live in a Monad contract, and only her key can change them.

scenes.title:
The agent proposes.
The contract checks.
scenes.sub: Signed menu · cheapest match · paid to the registered counter · settled in under a second
scenes.vo: At the counter she scans a menu the café signed. She says oat latte. Her agent, behind a context firewall, sees only items and prices, picks the cheapest match, and Tally's contract checks every rule before a cent moves. Paid in under a second.

scenes.title:
Pricier?
It waits for you.
scenes.sub: $1.40 more than the cheapest coffee → her Face ID, or nothing moves.
scenes.vo: If the agent is talked into the large one, the contract won't let it pay alone. It's one dollar forty more than the cheapest coffee, so Tally waits for Riya's Face ID.

scenes.title:
Mom tops it up.
In a second.
scenes.sub: One link · passkey · AUSD · fee $0.00 · “For lunches this week”
scenes.vo: Back in Pune, her mom opens a link, uses her fingerprint, and sends twenty dollars with a note: for lunches this week. It arrives in about a second, in dollars, and it can only be spent the way the rules allow.

scenes.title:
Attack your
own agent.
scenes.sub: Fake counter · phantom fee · price ×2 · upsell. Four attacks, four reverts.
scenes.vo: Don't take our word for it. Attack your own agent: a fake counter, a phantom fee, a doubled price, an upsell. All four reach the contract, and all four are refused.

scenes.title:
Every payment,
on the record.
scenes.sub: Receipts, family top-ups, blocked attempts and points, indexed by Envio.
scenes.vo: Every payment, top-up and blocked attempt is on the record, indexed by Envio, with points for real purchases only.

scenes.title:
Same passkey.
Open a counter.
scenes.sub: Your Face ID signs the menu. A bond proves you're honest.
scenes.vo: Any café can join. The same passkey signs its menu, and a bond that anyone can slash keeps the menu honest.

scenes.title:
Three proofs,
one transaction.
scenes.vo: Here's how it fits together. One passkey gives the owner key and a capped agent key. The café signs its menu. The agent proposes one item from behind a firewall. Then a single Monad transaction checks the signature, the Merkle proof for the item and price, and the family's rules, and pays only the counter's registered account. Envio indexes every receipt.

scenes.title:
Fast enough
for a coffee.

stats: welcome credit, built for the reserve-balance rule

scenes.vo: Why Monad? Payments settle in under a second, so tap and go is honest, and fees are small enough for a two dollar chai. We even built our sponsor around Monad's reserve balance rule, sending each welcome in a single transaction.

scenes.title: Real, on Monad.

cards.line: Sourcify-verified contract · 32 contract tests · settled in 0.6 s
One passkey → owner, agent and counter keys
fund(id, amount, note) · family top-up arrives in a second
Hosted HyperIndex serving payments and top-ups
kimi-k2.6 picks an item id; rules fallback
APK on a Moto G34 · Digital Asset Links verified

scenes.vo: And it's real. A Sourcify-verified contract on Monad testnet, thirty-two contract tests and sixty-five app tests. Mera derives every key from one passkey. AUSD top-ups carry a purpose note. Envio indexes the history. Kimi picks behind a firewall. And it runs as an Android app on a real phone.

scenes.title: Tally controls the item.
scenes.vo: Greenlight controls the store. AP2 controls the cart. Tally controls the item.
